# chdverify

[← Command index](README.md)

Check CHD files against their internal SHA-1 checksums with chdman.

## Synopsis

```
chdverify [options]
```

## Description

Finds every `.chd` file under the input path (or takes the one file given) and runs
`chdman verify` on it. A CHD passes when chdman reports that the overall SHA-1
verification succeeded. The run stops with an error at the first CHD that fails.

Nothing is written or changed.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | A `.chd` file, or a directory searched recursively for them; must exist. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Verify every CHD in a folder

```bash
chdverify -i /path/to/chds
```

### Verify one CHD without the confirmation prompt

```bash
chdverify -i "/path/to/Game (USA).chd" --no-preview
```

## Notes

- `-p` does not skip the check; chdman still reads every CHD.
- chdman (MameChdman) must be installed as a JoyBox tool.
